content:
A temporary explanation in a different language:

DECIDUOUS is a platform experiment (in the economic sense, in that it plays a kind of developmental matchmaker between you and me) which guesses that art operates with a type of informal logic (measured in aesthetics and poetics) which stashes a kind of continuous ambivalence within discrete material things. This proposes that art of this kind involves setting-aside of the chance of communication through forms.

It is a platform experiment like an incunabula, meaning that it can only swaddle the slightest sense of this type of logic.

This stashing, I guess, resembles how knowledge is stashed in things like books and algorithms and other tools. (We think of the thing, the book, in the material world, and its knowledge as somewhere off to the side.) And this platform guesses that the discrete material ambivalence of an artwork can itself work like that type of stashed knowledge, i.e., be of use, in the continuous and incompleteable metabolism of the human world.

DECIDUOUS most of the time looks like a physically hamstrung nothing-at-all; you have to see it in a particular light. At least it is a piece of software that is at least designed to support the least of this kind of guessed-at informal logic. This isn't a revolutionary design, but is just different enough to allow some difference in use. It's designed as a replacement (something in lieu) of a number of tools and formal concepts—some outmoded, like herbal codices, and some contemporary, like the Internet-as-of-now.

The platform is expressed by it first instantiation, which you are reading. I add to it when I can. Often things are rewritten, which is what will happen to this page.

The body of this first instantiation is a series of documents which record experimental approaches.
title: Platform reading

content:
The DECIDUOUS- corpus is a body of documents which mirrors recursively the organisational Body responsible for maintaining it; does this restlessly;

it is commonly used to train aesthetic dislocation algorithms, which study the deconvolution of how an outside stopped thing affects inside a person in motion. These algorithms categorically approach a 99% error rate; aren't recommended for use in production;

the corpus can be transformed by componentisation or hygiene against WordNet, a lexical database of words-we-have-agreed-on; please note

this is one of a nearly-infinite "real-world" corpora, and will almost certainly contain missing or incomplete fields, wild pointers, incoherent data. Not enough to not imagine it does not. But no it is almost as certainly "not real-world," is afterwards in proportion, counter, exo: itself an outside stopped thing; the body members are air-gapped from the thick of it;

there's gaps too inside the oily document-responsible bodies. And thatches of loss. Still we ask questions of corpora and their answers ring as bells. You might ask this one: what's changed? What could it have been like now, before it was like this now? What is the convolution of this other possible row of nows with the falloff of our outside afterwards now?

but there is a known issue anyway of overdimensionality in working with deciduity. Asking "what's changed?" causes the corpus to faint. And shed its schema and content sharply. So becomes headless.
